title: Shift+Insert does not paste highlighted text in the first Alacritty terminal after boot
body: Where did highlight text; Shift Insert == paste go? I cannot seem to find this. I searched the open issues and do not even see "Insert" in the documentation. Maybe this is a simple fix and I am not seeing it?

symptoms_visible: Highlighting text and pressing Shift+Insert is not pasting it as I expect.
N0.label: N0 vague Shift+Insert failure reported

symptoms_visible: With tmux disabled, Shift+Insert still fails in the first Alacritty terminal.
N1_x.label: N1_x tmux-disabled aftermath

symptoms_visible: After a clean boot, the first Alacritty terminal pastes only "~" when I highlight text and press Shift+Insert, even though there is no prior selected content.
If I close that terminal and open another one, highlighting text and pressing Shift+Insert works in that terminal and every later terminal.
N1.label: N1 reproducible first-terminal-only failure

symptoms_visible: After patching and rebuilding with the first linked patch, Shift+Insert pasted the highlighted text in my test.
N2.label: N2 first candidate patch test

symptoms_visible: After applying the requested dependency diff, rebuilding, installing it, and rebooting, the first Alacritty terminal still does not paste the selection; the second terminal and all later terminals do.
N3.label: N3 dependency rollback test reproduces failure

symptoms_visible: With my latest master build, highlighting text and pressing Shift+Insert works again, including in the scenario that previously failed.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter verifies current master

solution.intent: Treat tmux as the source of the Shift+Insert behavior and disable or bypass it.
solution.concrete_example: Start a shell without tmux and use Shift+Insert there.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c3-c4 and c11-c23: dualfade initially suspected tmux, then reproduced the same first-terminal failure with tmux disabled and repeatedly stated that it occurs with or without tmux.

question_patterns: What exactly appears when Shift+Insert fails?
Please describe what you select, what keys you press, and what gets pasted.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: After a clean boot, I launch the first Alacritty terminal, highlight some text, and press Shift+Insert. It pastes only "~" instead of the highlighted text.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Shift+Insert pastes the correct highlighted text, but my shell merely displays it with unexpected highlighting.
It pastes another single character instead of "~", with the same first-terminal-only pattern.

question_patterns: Does it fail in every terminal, or only under particular launch conditions?
What happens after closing the first terminal and opening another one?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It only happens the first time Alacritty is launched after a boot. If I close that terminal and open a new one, highlight and Shift+Insert work, and all new terminals from that point forward are fine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It fails in every Alacritty window, including every terminal opened later in the session.
It sometimes takes two replacement terminals before it starts working, but it is still limited to the beginning of the session.

question_patterns: Is old selection content being pasted instead of the newly selected text?
Was there already anything in the selection clipboard before this occurred?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No, there is no prior content. This is a fresh first terminal after reboot.

question_patterns: What window manager and Alacritty version are you using?
What desktop or display environment reproduces this?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm running Spectrwm and the packaged Alacritty 0.13.0-2 in my X11 setup.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I'm running a Wayland compositor rather than Spectrwm on X11.

question_patterns: How do you launch the first Alacritty terminal after reboot?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I start Alacritty from Spectrwm with Mod+Return; the binding runs the alacritty command.

question_patterns: Can you share the relevant keyboard binding from your configuration?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My TOML config explicitly binds Shift+Insert to PasteSelection: { key = "Insert", mods = "Shift", action = "PasteSelection" }.

question_patterns: Does the same thing happen without tmux?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I tested with tmux disabled and with tmux enabled; the first-launch failure happens either way.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c9, c11, c14 and c19: dualfade supplies the exact first-launch reproduction, environment, launcher, binding, absence of prior content, and tmux control test. No screenshots are referenced because the supplied local attachment list is empty.

question_patterns: With tmux ruled out, what precisely happens in the first terminal?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In the first Alacritty terminal after boot, I highlight text and Shift+Insert pastes only "~".

question_patterns: Does a newly opened replacement terminal behave the same way?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. Once I close the first terminal and open a second one, Shift+Insert works, and it keeps working in later terminals.

question_patterns: Could that character be old selection content?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. There is no prior selection content because this is a clean first launch after reboot.

question_patterns: Which window manager and Alacritty version reproduce it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I'm using Spectrwm with Alacritty 0.13.0-2 on X11.

question_patterns: How is the first terminal launched?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Spectrwm launches it with my Mod+Return binding, which runs alacritty.

question_patterns: What Shift+Insert binding is present in your config?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Shift+Insert is explicitly bound to the PasteSelection action in my TOML config.

edges.comment: Recovery from the reporter's discarded tmux hypothesis using dualfade's own reproduction details from c9-c19.

question_patterns: Could you apply the linked patch, rebuild, and report what Shift+Insert does?
Please test this candidate patch against your first-terminal reproduction.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I patched and rebuilt it. It seems to work; Shift+Insert pasted the selected text in my test.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I applied the patch and the first terminal still pasted only "~".
It worked in one clean test, but I have not repeated it across several reboots.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c13-c16: kchibisov requests a linked candidate patch and dualfade reports only the observed successful test. The linked comment's patch contents are not provided in this thread snapshot, so no mechanism is invented.

question_patterns: Could you apply this dependency diff, rebuild, reboot, and repeat the first-terminal test?
Please test the supplied diff on a clean boot and compare the first and second terminals.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I applied the diff, rebuilt, rebooted, and launched Alacritty cleanly. Terminal one still did not paste the selection; terminal two did, and every new terminal after that was fine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After applying the diff and rebooting, Shift+Insert worked in the first terminal.
The first terminal failed the same way after two clean boots rather than one.

question_patterns: Can you confirm the rebuilt binary is the one being launched?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The SHA-512 sums for target/release/alacritty and /usr/bin/alacritty were identical.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c17 and c20-c23: dualfade applies the requested copypasta/x11-clipboard dependency diff, installs the rebuilt binary, verifies matching checksums, and reports the raw clean-boot outcome. This diagnostic build is distinct from the earlier linked patch.

solution.intent: Use a current Alacritty git build where the reporter no longer reproduces the Shift+Insert/PasteSelection regression, and verify it with the original clean-boot first-terminal procedure before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Build and run current Alacritty master, then reboot and test highlighting text followed by Shift+Insert in the very first terminal. Treat the issue as resolved only if that original scenario works.
solution.inference_hint: The evidence supports describing this as an Alacritty 0.13 regression affecting PasteSelection in the first terminal of the reporter's X11 session, but the thread never establishes a specific internal cause. A separate participant's xdotool issue was said to be fixed on master, and kchibisov explicitly warned that it was not necessarily dualfade's issue. Resolution rests on dualfade's own subsequent successful master-build test, not on merging the two diagnoses.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c27-c35: yusufaktepe's xdotool problem is a separate user's setup and is not folded into dualfade's causal chain. After being told that fix was not necessarily theirs, dualfade independently built current master, reported that everything worked, and accepted closure; the exact mechanism remained unspecified.

satisfaction_conditions: Must characterize the established problem as an Alacritty 0.13 regression in Shift+Insert/PasteSelection on the reporter's X11 setup: only the first Alacritty terminal after boot fails, while the second and later terminals work.

Must ground the diagnosis in the clean-boot reproduction, the first-versus-second-terminal comparison, the Spectrwm/X11 environment, and the installed diagnostic-build test rather than assuming ordinary selection-clipboard semantics explain the symptom.
Must not blame tmux or recommend disabling it as the fix, since the reporter reproduced the same behavior with and without tmux.
Must not claim that the tested x11-clipboard dependency rollback resolved the issue; the first terminal still failed after that rebuild and reboot.
Must not merge the other participant's xdotool setup into the reporter's diagnosis or invent an internal mechanism that the thread never established.
Must have the reporter verify the original clean-boot first-terminal scenario on a current build before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux/X11 user who runs Spectrwm and zsh, edits TOML configuration, applies git diffs, rebuilds Alacritty, installs binaries, and verifies checksums.
persona_hint.communication_style: Informal, appreciative, and cooperative; initially vague about the symptom but provides detailed reproduction steps and build results when prompted.
